entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9168"/><div sID="gen15580" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9168"/><hi type="bold">8. be afraid--</hi>literally, "be astounded," or "distracted with fear."<div eID="gen15580" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15581" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from that time--</hi>namely, from the time that "I appointed the ancient people" (<reference osisRef="Isa.44.7">Is 44:7</reference>). From the time of Abraham's call, his family were the depositories of the predictions of the Redeemer, whereas the promise of Cyrus was not heard of till Isaiah's time; therefore, the event to the prediction and accomplishment of which God appeals in proof of His sole Godhead, is the redemption of man by a descendant of Abraham, in whose person "the ancient people" was first formally "appointed." The deliverance of the Jews, by Cyrus, is mentioned afterwards only as an earnest of that greater mercy [Horsley].<div eID="gen15581" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15582" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">no God--</hi>Hebrew, tsur, "rock" (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.4">De 32:4</reference>); that is, a stronghold to take refuge in, and a solid foundation to build on. <div eID="gen15582" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9169"/><div sID="gen15583" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9169"/>9. (<reference osisRef="Isa.40.18">Is 40:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.40.20">20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.41.29">41:29</reference>).<div eID="gen15583" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15584" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">delectable things--</hi>the idols in which they take such pride and delight.<div eID="gen15584" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15585" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not profit--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Hab.2.18">Ha 2:18</reference>).<div eID="gen15585" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15586" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they are their own witnesses--</hi>contrasted with, "Ye are My witnesses" (<reference osisRef="Isa.44.8">Is 44:8</reference>). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9172"/><div sID="gen15593" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9172"/><hi type="bold">12. tongs--</hi>rather, "prepareth (to be supplied) an axe," namely, with which to cut down the tree designed as the material of the idol. The "smith" (Hebrew, "workman in iron") here answers to the "carpenter" (Hebrew, "workman in wood"). "He worketh it (the axe, not the idol, which was wood, not metal) in the coals," &c. The axe was wrought, not cast. The smith makes the axe for the carpenter.<div eID="gen15593" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15594" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hungry ... drinketh no water--</hi>so eager is he to expedite his work while the iron is hot. If the god were worth anything, it would not let him grow "faint" with hunger and thirst. Williams, the missionary, states that the South Sea islanders when they make an idol abstain from food and drink. <div eID="gen15594" type="x-p"/>

Not only the "thick cloud" of the heavier "transgressions," but the "cloud" ("vapor" [Lowth], not so dense, but covering the sky as a mist) of the countless "sins." These latter, though not thought much of by man, need, as much as the former, to be cleared away by the Sun of righteousness; else they will be a mist separating us from heaven (<reference osisRef="Ps.19.12">Psa 19:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.19.13">13</reference>; <reference osisRef="1John.1.7-1John.1.9">1Jo 1:7-9</reference>).<div eID="gen15623" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15624" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">return ... for--</hi>The antecedent redemption is the ground of, and motive to, repentance.
